statement: Let C(k,i) = sum over j with 0 <= j < k and queries[j][0] <= i <= queries[j][1] of queries[j][2], for 0 <= k <= len(queries) and 0 <= i < len(nums) (the empty sum is 0). The function returns a result r, and exactly one of the following holds. (a) r = -1 and for every k with 0 <= k <= len(queries) there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] > C(k,i). (b) 0 <= r <= len(queries), for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) we have nums[i] <= C(r,i), and for every k with 0 <= k < r there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] > C(k,i).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(queries). The preconditions are 1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= nums[i] <= 500000 for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= m <= 100000, and for every j with 0 <= j < m, len(queries[j]) = 3; writing queries[j] = [l_j, r_j, val_j], we have 0 <= l_j <= r_j < n and 1 <= val_j <= 5.
